q: When bodies are immersed in a liquid there is ____ in weight.
e: An immersed body experiences an upward force that counteracts gravity, making it appear lighter.

q: This is because of a property of liquids called ____.
e: Buoyancy is the upward force exerted by any fluid upon a body placed in it.

q: Since buoyant force is directed upward, it is called ____.
e: Upward thrust is another term for the buoyant force acting opposite to the direction of gravity.

q: Archimedes' principle states that the upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed in a liquid is equal to the ____ of the liquid displaced by the body.
e: This is the fundamental statement of Archimedes' principle, relating buoyant force to the displaced fluid's weight.

q: Archimedes' principle is true not only for liquids but also for ____.
e: Buoyancy applies to all fluids, including gases like air, which is why helium balloons rise.

q: The weight of a body when it is immersed in a liquid is called ____.
e: Apparent weight is the measured weight of an object in a fluid, which is less than its true weight in a vacuum or air.

q: It is less than the actual weight of the body because of ____ of the liquid acting on it.
e: The upward thrust partially supports the object, reducing the net downward force measured as weight.

q: A body will float in a liquid (fluid) if the upward thrust acting on it is ____ to its weight.
e: Flotation occurs when the buoyant force exactly balances the gravitational force on the object.

q: If the weight of the body is greater than the upward thrust, the body will ____.
e: A net downward force causes the object to accelerate towards the bottom of the fluid.

q: If the weight is smaller than the upward thrust, the body will ____ up to the surface.
e: A net upward force causes the object to accelerate towards the surface of the fluid.

q: Since the body is in equilibrium, the net force acting on it is ____.
e: For a floating body, the upward buoyant force and downward gravitational force cancel each other out.

q: According to Eq. (3.8), the ratio of the densities is equal to the ratio of the immersed volume to the ____ of the whole body.
e: The fraction of an object's volume that is submerged is equal to the ratio of the object's density to the fluid's density.
